## Motivation

On a multi-GPU LTX server every decode-parallel rank runs the VAE decode, so that the spatial-parallel convolutions can exchange halo rows. `_decode_spatial` only takes that height split when each rank's rows fit in one tile. Otherwise it falls back to `tiled_decode` with the split disabled, and every rank then decodes every tile of the whole frame. On two GPUs both ranks do the same work, and the second GPU adds nothing.

After warmup, `check_invalid_values_in_kv_cache(fill_with_zero=True)` scans every KV cache buffer for NaN/Inf, then zeroes it. items.body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend resolves a request's I/O-backed media on the API runtime before multimodal dispatch (`core::prefetch`), but it only knows `http(s)://`, `file://` and absolute paths. Any other string counts as inline base64, so a request naming its media by some other URI scheme (`custom://bucket/key`, for example) reaches the MM worker as "base64", fails to decode there, and the client gets a 500 (`encode failed`) rather than a 400. An external `MmProcessor` also has no way to refuse media it cannot encode (an unsupported modality, say) before the request is fetched and queued

items.title: [Perf] dsv41: Read Engram rows from peer device shards
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Opt-in Triton kernel reads Engram rows directly from peer device shards, eliminating all-gather and global buffer overhead for wide-TP decode.
items.body:
With per-rank Engram tables and DP attention, every lookup all-gathers all DP ranks' hash ids, gathers the owned rows for all of them into a `[DP x tokens]` bf16 buffer, and reduce-scatters it back. The traffic and the buffer grow with the DP size, so wide-EP decode pays a collective per Engram layer that is larger than the lookup itself.

This adds an opt-in path, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_PEER_SHARDS=1`:

- Each TP rank keeps its row shard in exportable device memory (CUDA VMM) and maps every peer's shard after loading: FABRIC handles across an NVLink domain (MNNVL), POSIX fds within a host.

## Description

Aggregated Helix prefill runs the full prompt on every context-parallel (CP) rank for attention, but each rank must persist only the compressed MLA KV records in the cache pages it owns. items.title: [Feature][KV Connector][Mooncake] Decode-to-prefill KV reuse for multi-turn P/D
items.author: slokesha
items.summary: In multi-turn P/D serving, the next turn's prompt starts with the previous prompt plus the tokens the decoder just generated. Only the decoder has that KV, so the prefiller recomputes it every turn. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

In multi-turn P/D serving, the next turn's prompt starts with the previous prompt plus the tokens the decoder just generated. Only the decoder has that KV, so the prefiller recomputes it every turn. This PR lets a `kv_both` prefiller **pull it from the decoder** over the existing Mooncake transfer engine. A router opts in per request through `kv_transfer_params`; requests without the new keys are unaffected.

Related: the MooncakeConnector RFC #60523. It doesn't cover this, and it notes that the hybrid Mamba/GDN path is fragile; this PR works for hybrid models.

items.body:
## Motivation

items.title: [Core][CUDA Graph] Separate prefill (token) and decode (request) CUDA graph capture sizes
items.author: Pb314314
items.summary: A batch with no graph of its size runs eagerly, and at serving batch sizes the CPU launching kernels, not the GPU, sets its speed. In model runner V2, one token list decides which batch sizes get graphs, for both prefill and decode.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Problem.** A CUDA graph replays a recorded step so the CPU does not launch each kernel. A batch with no graph of its size runs eagerly, and at serving batch sizes the CPU launching kernels, not the GPU, sets its speed. In model runner V2, one token list decides which batch sizes get graphs, for both prefill and decode. With speculative decoding each decode request carries 1 + K tokens, so a 1024-token list covers only 1024/(1+K) decode requests: 128 at K=7, while servers run up to 1024. On GB200, the models we validated spend 22–73% of engine time

items.title: [ROCm][Quantization] Add int8 per-channel lm_head quantization for RDNA (gfx11/gfx12)
items.author: zohaibm-amd
items.summary: Adds int8 per-channel lm_head quantization for RDNA GPUs, halving bandwidth-bound decode cost while preserving bf16 accuracy, building on prior W4A16 work.
items.body:
Builds on #62708. It adds a second value to `KernelConfig.lm_head_quantization`: `int8_per_channel`. At load time, an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head is quantized to symmetric int8 with one scale per output channel, then run on a new RDNA W8A16 op.

Many 4-bit checkpoints leave the lm_head in fp16/bf16. Decode reads the whole head on every step, so on bandwidth-bound RDNA it is often one of the largest per-token costs. Int8 halves that read. Int4 (#62708) cuts it further, but int8 keeps accuracy at the bf16 level, which lets users trade speed against accuracy.

items.summary: On ROCm, vLLM reserves about 6x more memory for CUDA graphs than they use, and takes the difference from the KV cache. The graph estimate comes from free memory, and on ROCm free memory counts every allocation as at least 2 MB.
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, vLLM reserves about 6x more memory for CUDA graphs than they use, and takes the difference from the KV cache. The graph estimate comes from free memory (`hipMemGetInfo`), and on ROCm free memory counts every allocation as at least 2 MB. HIP makes a small kernel-argument allocation for each captured graph, so approximately: 1,700 graphs look like 3.7 GB while the card's own counter grows by 0.66 GB (Llama 3.1 8B instruct)

This PR takes the same measurements from this process's exact VRAM counter, DRM fdinfo (`/proc/self/fdinfo`), where the platform has one.

items.title: [Fix] diffusion/serving: Reclaim abandoned shared-memory replies
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Fixes shared-memory leak in diffusion scheduler by scoping reply files to per-RPC private directories with atomic cleanup on cancellation/timeout.
items.body:
## Summary

Large local scheduler replies are spilled to `/dev/shm`, but only the receiving client removes them. If an RPC times out or is cancelled before the reply arrives, the scheduler still writes the result and no process deletes it. Repeated abandoned frame-return RPCs can exhaust shared memory.

- Scope reply files to a private directory owned by each sync/async RPC. Advertise its opaque name through the existing local ZMQ routing identity; no request payload or model changes.
- Retire the directory atomically before cleanup so a late producer cannot create new files during deletion.

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Reject incomplete NIXL cache files before reading
items.author: AEGO-WRJ
items.summary: A failed NIXL write can leave an empty or truncated cache file. The current lookup treats any existing file as a hit, and NIXL 1.4.0 can report a short read as successful.
items.body:
## Motivation

Refs #45563. A failed NIXL write can leave an empty or truncated cache file. The current lookup treats any existing file as a hit, and NIXL 1.4.0 can report a short read as successful. This lets a restore publish incomplete KV or sidecar data. The issue reports incorrect DSA outputs after restoring empty indexer files.

Lookup checks alone are insufficient: hybrid restores using `assume_stored` can skip lookup. Validate the requested byte count at the shared read entrypoint before starting a transfer.

## Modifications

- Treat empty FILE objects as lookup misses.
- Reject FILE

`LTX2Pipeline._unmerge_stage1_distilled_from_base` (`runtime/pipelines/ltx_2_pipeline.py`) restores the base by merging the stage-1 distilled LoRA again with strength `-s`, then calling `commit_merged_as_base()`.

items.author: YLlllllllllll

items.body:
## Overview

FIX #63358

A Hermes response can contain a valid `<tool_call>` and then a later region that is not a call. Non-streaming parsing dropped every call, and streaming never sent the text after the bad region. items.summary: Enables FlashAttention-4 for head sizes that are multiples of 8 up to 128 on Blackwell, eliminating costly sm80 FA2 fallback for models like Qwen-VL with head sizes 72/80.

The CUDA platform decides whether FlashAttention can serve a layer with `FlashAttentionBackend.get_supported_head_sizes()`. That is FA3's list: 32, 64, 96, ..., 256. items.title: [Perf] diffusion: Write uncompressed PNG responses without Pillow's row filters
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Bypasses Pillow's adaptive PNG row filter when compress_level=0, writing unfiltered rows directly via zlib to reduce image response latency in diffusion serving.
items.body:
## Motivation

Image responses are encoded as PNG with zlib level 0 by default since #45987. Pillow still runs its adaptive row filter at that level: for every row it tries the PNG filters and keeps the one with the smallest sum (the encoded files use filters 1 and 2). At level 0 the deflate stream is stored, not compressed, so the filter cannot make the file smaller. It only costs time, and the time is on the output rank between the end of the forward and the reply:

| frame | Pillow, `compress_level=0` | unfiltered rows in stored blocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1024x1024 RGBA (Qwen-Image-2.1) | 74.

items.title: [RFC]: Keep per-request token lists out of EngineCore garbage collection
items.author: gcanlin
items.summary: Removes per-request token-id lists from CPython GC tracking to eliminate O(tokens) pauses causing up to 17% idle time in distributed decode inference under pipeline parallelism.
items.body:
### Motivation.

Each `Request` in EngineCore holds its prompt twice as Python `list[int]`: `prompt_token_ids` and the copy `_all_token_ids`. CPython's cyclic GC visits every element of every tracked list, so each gen-0/gen-1 collection costs O(tokens of the requests that arrived since the previous collection). Long prompts make these pauses long. Under DP the cost multiplies, because all ranks run in lockstep and a pause on any one rank stalls the whole group.

items.author: zcnrex
items.summary: DeepGEMM's Mega MoE picks its tile from the calling rank's own token count. With DP attention and EP, an eager prefill forward can be very uneven across ranks.

## Motivation

DeepGEMM's Mega MoE picks its tile (`block_m`) from the calling rank's own token count. With DP attention and EP, an eager prefill forward can be very uneven across ranks. The whole fused dispatch-GEMM-combine kernel runs at the pace of the badly tiled ranks.

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
items.author: Woody-Hu
items.summary: transposes the activations into the layout expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to dense operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.
items.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 m

items.title: [Bugfix][CPU] Match GPU conv-state layout in GDN spec decode
items.author: JaredforReal
items.summary: Fixes CPU speculative decode crash in GDN by aligning conv-state tensor layout with the GPU path, resolving mismatches on short or partial token rows.
items.body:
## Overview

On CPU, the GDN speculative-decode path updates the conv state with a different layout from the GPU `causal_conv1d_update`. The two agree only when a row has the full `num_spec + 1` tokens. Any shorter row, such as one where the drafter proposed fewer tokens, or a decode row with no drafts that MRV2 still keeps as a spec row, makes the next step read the wrong conv history. If the previous step accepted more tokens than the row now has, it crashes:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (6) must match the size of tensor b (5) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Muse Spark: column-shard the MoE pooler/unpooler over TP
items.author: fanxingran
items.summary: Converts Muse Spark MoE pooler/unpooler from ReplicatedLinear to ColumnParallelLinear over TP, reducing per-GPU memory by 6.8 GiB and improving throughput/latency on ROCm.
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the Muse Spark MoE pooler (8192 → 4096) and unpooler (4096 → 8192) are `ReplicatedLinear`, so at TP8 every rank reads both full BF16 weights on every step: 134 MB per layer, about 8.3 GB per forward over the 62 layers. This PR makes both projections `ColumnParallelLinear` and all-gathers their output columns over TP. Each output column is still computed from the full reduction on one rank; the gather only moves data. Each rank holds `1 / TP` of the weights, which frees 6.8 GiB per GPU for the KV cache.

### What does this PR do?

## Overview

Call `gc.freeze()` in `EngineCore` after a scheduling step that admits new requests, follows a request's arrival, or runs while requests wait. Without it, each full (gen-2) GC pass traverses every live request's token lists and KV block lists. ## Overview

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Muse Spark: finalize the token-sharded MoE reduction in one reduce-scatter
items.author: fanxingran
items.summary: On ROCm under TP, finalizes the MoE output of a batch of at least 256 tokens in three steps: reduce-scatter, per-rank, then all-gather. It does this in 1024-token chunks. [Discussion: @jeejeelee @tjtanaa @hongxiayang Could you take a look when you have time?]
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm under TP, `MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce` finalizes the MoE output of a batch of at least 256 tokens in three steps: reduce-scatter, per-rank `fused_post_expert_finalize`, then all-gather. It does this in 1024-token chunks. With `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16` (the AMD Day 0 recipe) the chunks bound no memory, so this PR finalizes the whole batch with one reduce-scatter and one all-gather per MoE layer. ## Description

In adaptive mode, the MiniMax-M3 chat template ends the prompt at the assistant header without prefilling `<mm:think>` or `</mm:think>`, and the model emits its own tags. The server resolves the reasoning mode from the end of the rendered prompt, but returned nothing for such a prompt, so the request's own `enable_thinking` reached `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser`. The template never reads that key. The Anthropic adapter sets it for `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`, so the parser prepended `<mm:think>` to output that already opened with one, and the tag leaked into the thinking block.

After the indexer scores a MiniMax-M3 context chunk, each (token, index head) row picks its 16 highest-scoring 128-token blocks. `minimax_m3_select_blocks` reads each row on its own, strided by the token count, because the scores are stored token-contiguous. items.summary: An RFC proposing optional teacher-generated rollouts for on-policy distillation, allowing batch-level selection between teacher and student data sources.
items.body:
### Feature request

Allow distillation to train on teacher-generated responses as well as student-generated ones. A user function chooses one source for each training batch. The existing teacher server generates teacher responses, then scores the complete sequences for the student's supervised distillation loss.

### Motivation

Today, OPD generates responses with the student and uses the teacher for scoring. Choosing the source within a run would let users start with teacher responses, mix both sources, or gradually switch to student-generated data without a separate generation/SFT/checkpoin

items.body:
The kernel computes the activation and per-block amax in fp32, while the reference rounds the GEMM output and the Relu2 output to bf16 before fp4_quantize. Verified locally on GB300 and B200 by repeating each case with fresh random inputs (failures / runs)

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6900756][perf] KVCMv2: fill the initial host tier in parallel, populate in 4 MiB calls
items.author: thorjohnsen
items.summary:
A KVCMv2 host tier is filled by one worker thread per. It goes 512 MiB at a time: the step open, prefault it with one call, then register it. [Discussion: 🎉
ℹ️ Recent review info
<]
items.body:
## Description

A KVCMv2 host tier is filled by one worker thread per `HostMem`. It goes 512 MiB at a time: `mprotect` the step open, prefault it with one `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` call, then register it. This PR changes two things:

1. **Prefault in 4 MiB calls (every fill).** A `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` call holds the process's `mmap_lock` for reading until it returns. Everything that needs the lock for writing waits behind it: the other pool's `mprotect` and registrations, and allocations on the executor. One call per 512 MiB step makes those waits long.
2. **Prefault the initial fill in parallel.*

## Summary

Adds an opt-in `token_order: morton` knob to `SolAttentionConfig`. # HybridEP retains dispatch metadata after combine

## Problem

`_HybridEPManager.combine()` clears `self.handle`, but leaves `routing_map`, `token_probs`, and `dispatched_probs` on the manager.
The manager no longer needs these fields after combine.

`dispatched_probs` is an autograd output whose context retains a dispatch handle.
That handle holds dispatch metadata.
Thus, clearing `self.handle` alone does not remove the manager's reference to that metadata.

### What does this PR do?

Fix `NIXLCheckpointEngine.build_topology` for a topology with one rollout worker.

`next_agent_metadata` used a negative slice start. When
`rollout_world_size == 1`, that evaluates to `0`, returning all metadata
instead of no successor metadata and causing `build_process_group` to fail:

    AssertionError: rollout_kwargs[next_agent_metadata] must have length of 1

Use an index relative to `len(metadata)` instead. Topologies with two or more
rollout workers retain the same slice bounds.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

End-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell: Megatron training with Transformer Engine's MXFP8 recipe, and an MXFP8 rollout on vLLM or SGLang whose weights the trainer quantizes with the learner's block rule. items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.title: Batch packed MTP context-parallel boundary exchanges
items.author: yashaswikarnati
items.summary: Packed MTP currently exchanges CP boundary tokens once per document. This change batches all documents into one boundary vector per neighbor per roll, and vectorizes local packed rolls and HSM boundary translation.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

Packed MTP currently exchanges CP boundary tokens once per document. This change batches all documents into one boundary vector per neighbor per roll, and vectorizes local packed rolls and HSM boundary translation.

items.title: fix(inference): bound batch-invariant MoE work by live rows, not worst-case buffers
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Batch-invariant (BI) inference with MXFP8 routed experts does work proportional to on every decode step, whatever the number of live tokens. This PR bounds that work by the live rows, which the kernels already read on device.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Batch-invariant (BI) inference with MXFP8 routed experts does work proportional to `max_tokens` on every decode step, whatever the number of live tokens. This PR bounds that work by the live rows, which the kernels already read on device. CUDA graphs keep their static shapes, and the quantized and reduced rows are bitwise unchanged.

It also removes an illegal memory access. The MXFP8 quantize kernel indexes rows in int32, so a worst-case buffer of 2^31 elements or more faults (see Problem).

items.title: fix(inference): opt-in float64 race noise for exact low-probability sampling
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Adds an opt-in for the torch sampling backend. When it is on, low-probability tokens are drawn at their softmax rate: float64 race noise moves the representable tail from about 20 nats below a row's top token to about 40 nats.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Prevent MFSDP v2 OOMs during initialization or CUDA graph capture caused by excessive MXFP8 buffer padding when an FSDP unit contains weights with different row widths.

MXFP8 block-atomic layouts align each data-parallel shard to 32 rows of every tensor in a parameter group. Grouping only by dtype and `requires_grad` makes this alignment depend on the least common multiple of unrelated row widths. items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

finalize_model_grads() scales gradients by 1 / num_tokens as a 0-D CUDA tensor so the step stays CUDA-graph safe. `grad_data *= scaling_factor` then runs PyTorch's broadcasting, dtype-casting elementwise kernel, which reaches only ~1.5 TB/s for BF16 grad buffers on GB300.

Scale grad_data and the extra main grads with torch._foreach_mul_, casting the factor to each tensor dtype so the fused path is taken. # What does this PR do?

With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks. For CP2 rank 0, length 64 caches positions `0…15, 48…63`, but length 32 needs `0…7, 24…31`. Taking a prefix of the old cache gives the wrong positions.

Rebuild the cache when a non-packed sequence shrinks with CP > 1. CP1 and packed inputs can still reuse the cache.

Fixes #8046.

## What

`DistributedOptimizer.load_state_dict` enters a populated-state branch when
`dist_checkpointing.load` has already filled the inner optimizer state in place
(via sharded-state-dict wrappers around the live state tensors). The previous
implementation passed the optimizer's own current state back through
`self.optimizer.load_state_dict`, which

- cleared `self.state` (PyTorch's `Optimizer.load_state_dict` does
  `self.state = defaultdict(dict)` unconditionally), and
- cast every state tensor to the param dtype, and (for TE `FusedAdam`)
  allocated fresh FP32 state copies.

items.title: fix(core): compare major version in experimental EOL check
items.author: NUAAwqy
items.summary: / decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the minor component of the version: Once mcore crosses a major boundary and the minor version resets to 0, this comparison can never fire again, so expired experimental APIs sil…
items.body:
`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:

```python
PkgVersion(introduced_with_version).minor + max_lifetime < PkgVersion(mcore_version).minor
```

Once mcore crosses a major boundary and the minor version resets to 0, this comparison can never fire again, so expired experimental APIs silently stop being flagged. items.title: [MoE] Opt-in EP-size-invariant expert combine (fixed fp32 reduction tree)
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout.
items.body:
**Problem.** Under `batch_invariant_mode`, the MoE combine sums each token's local expert outputs per EP rank, rounds that partial to fp32, and then adds the rank partials in rank order. Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout. That rules out, for example, training at EP8 while generating at EP4.

Measured on Nemotron-3-Nano (top-6, hidden 2688) in our RL setup, which uses the same combine:
- One MoE layer at EP2 vs EP1

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: honor teacher temperature in on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.author: linmuchuiyang
items.summary: nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.26.0 vectorises the output store by 2 and asserts for odd: Any real-length sequence hits it (first full-model log-prob pass, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers); synthetic tests with fixed even lengths do not. Fixed in cudnn-frontend #407 (2026…
items.body:
## What happens

Megatron-Core's DSV4 sparse attention calls cuDNN's DSL kernel with `top_k = min(index_topk, sk)` where `sk` is the
compressed KV length of the sequence (`csa_kernels._indexer_topk_core`). nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.26.0 vectorises the output

## 背景

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。


## 工作原理

此工作流在 `verl-project/verl` 仓库中运行，并使用**独立的私有 Fork 仓库**来存储翻译工具（Python 翻译引擎、技能/提示文档以及 `.po` 翻译记忆库）。这使得上游仓库保持整洁——它仅接收 `en/` 文档和工作流文件的更改。

**工作流步骤：**

1. **检出（Checkout）** Fork 私有仓库的 `main` 分支（包含 `translate_md.py`、`skill.md`、`.po` 缓存）。
2. **同步（Sync）** Fork 的 `main` 分支与最新的上游 `main` 分支（通过 `git merge`），然后将同步后的 `main` 分支推送回 Fork。
3. **翻译（Translate）** — 运行 `translate_md.py`，将每个中文文档拆分为块，复用 `.po` 文件中的缓存翻译，仅对更改/未翻译的块调用 OpenAI 兼容的

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. `Worker._setup_env_cuda_visible_devices()` pins this rank's accelerator only when a

relabeling devices so that index 0 is this rank's device.

it does not, every rank in the job runs on the same physical device. The collision does not

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Background

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.

items.title: fix: propagate fully async worker failures to training
items.author: heyxingxing
items.summary: Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups.
items.body:
Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups. Preserve the first failure and raise it in the consumer with its original cause; stop scheduling work, cancel in-flight tasks, and prevent automatic replacement of the failed worker. Explicit ABORTED retries and intentional shutdown cancellation keep their existing behavior.

Closes https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/2399

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.body:
Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

```
whitened_values = (values - global_mean) * rsqrt(var)
if not shift_mean:
    whitened_values += global_mean
```

That is not a scale-only path. This change makes `shift_mean` do what it says:

- `shift_mean=True` (default): `(values - global_mean) * rsqrt(global_var + epsilon)` — zero-mean, unit-variance
- `shift_mean=False`: `values * rsqrt(global_var + epsilon)` — scale only; do not subtract the mean, and do not add it back

items.title: fix: cancel pending rollout tasks after a failure
items.author: yuyz-cyber
items.summary: When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task except…
items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: preserve equals in extra environment values
items.author: imshunsuke
items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

## Summary

This PR makes Slime's external SGLang rollout path work with streaming `/generate` responses.

- incremental accumulation of tokens, logprobs, top-p metadata, routed-expert metadata, and response text
- validation that rejects malformed or mismatched stream formats instead of silently training on incomplete output

items.body:
Fixes #2268

## Problem

`slime/utils/reloadable_process_group.py::_wrap_low_level_call` runs a memory probe **before every wrapped collective**:

```python
def _wrap_low_level_call(check_memory=True):
    if check_memory:

        if mem_info["free_GB"] < 3:
            clear_memory()
    yield
```

# VIME External Draft Training Design

## 1. Background

VIME can already load an external EAGLE/DFlash/Dspark.. Draft model through vLLM's `SpeculativeConfig` for speculative decoding. However, online training currently only covers the MTP layers inside the Target model. As Target parameters change throughout RL training, an external Draft model gradually becomes misaligned. This lowers Draft-token acceptance and average acceptance length, and may
eventually make the additional Draft and verification cost larger than the speculative-decoding benefit.

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary
https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/issues/206
This PR adds end-to-end LoRA support for Megatron actor training with colocated vLLM rollout. When `--lora-rank > 0`, the training actor applies LoRA adapters via Megatron-Bridge, exports PEFT-format adapters after each weight update, and hot-loads them into vLLM through the runtime LoRA API. Rollout requests then use the adapter name instead of the base model path.

This enables parameter-efficient RL fine-tuning without full-weight sync between trainer and inference engines on every step.

items.title: [Bugfix][Training] Avoid entropy grad graph when entropy_coef is zero
items.author: Henry-Jessie
items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

## Description

Fixes #304

Importing any `rm_hub` submodule executes `vime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py`, which imports runtime-only deps at module level, so the reward CPU tests fail at pytest collection in lightweight environments. The chain is deeper than the issue's traceback shows: `aiohttp` (used by `remote_rm` only), `vime.utils.misc` / `vime.utils.types` (pull in `torch` and `httpx`), and `sympy` / `pylatexenc` at the top of `math_utils`.

## Changes

- `rm_hub/__init__.py`: defer `aiohttp` and `load_function` to their call sites; move `Sample` / `aiohttp` under `TYPE_CHECKING`

items.body:
`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.
